findings.title: Duplicate JSON keys erase external canary tokens before the marker oracle
findings.description: json.loads uses last-key-wins at both active-store reads. grant_flags serializes only the parsed object, so a raw active auth.json with unknown=external-token followed by unknown=clean reports external_marker_absent=true and passes require_flags. The resolver read-only byte-stability check preserves these bytes rather than detecting them. This is an observer false-green, not evidence of a real credential adopted by native Hermes.

actual.boundary: actual grant_flags + require_flags fed by actual json.loads; native NOT_RUN

findings.criterion: H02 canary observer sensitivity/fail-closed evidence; known external markers, including unknown fields, must not be silently discarded by decoding.
findings.minimal remedy: Reject duplicate JSON keys at the raw active-store decoding boundary (top-level and nested), or independently scan the raw UTF-8 bytes before parsing while retaining schema checks. Add raw-file duplicate-key positive/negative controls rather than another parsed-dict-only test.

findings.title: A swallowed SIGALRM timeout can still publish OBSERVED_SCOPED / exit 0
findings.description: The one-shot alarm handler only raises TimeoutError. Unlike attempted offline I/O, no independent fault flag is latched before raising. A reader that catches that exception can return a result, and main cancels the alarm and publishes success. A later hang also loses the claimed intrinsic 10-second finite bound. Pinned native readers contain broad except Exception seams, but no installed native hang or full runtime was executed here.

findings.criterion: Finite fail-closed observer; a deadline event cannot become clean success merely because the callee swallowed an exception.
findings.minimal remedy: Latch timeout occurrence before raising and require the latch to remain false before success publication. Require a parent-owned hard subprocess deadline and join/family readback for genuine stuck/native-call cases; this does not require a new generic supervisor. Add a caught-timeout regression and retain the outer hard-bound evidence as separate installed QA.

findings.title: Path checks and file read use different pathname resolutions
findings.description: is_symlink/stat/read_bytes are separated. Deterministic replacement of a checked regular file with a symlink after stat makes _read_fixed return another synthetic file. Compile-time paths prevent caller path injection, and readonly/exclusive parent mounts reduce exposure; this is a hardening finding, not proof that the approved OCI fixture or native writer performed such a replacement.

findings.criterion: The helper claims symlink refusal at every ancestor and bounded fixed-file reads. These checks should bind to the opened object where a writer can replace a pathname.
findings.minimal remedy: Open via trusted directory FDs with O_NOFOLLOW (and ancestor no-follow), validate fstat on the same descriptor, and read at most cap+1 bytes from that descriptor. Alternatively explicitly narrow this helper to parent-attested immutable/exclusive inputs and retain active-store race coverage before live acceptance.
